newsitem.title: INDIA: CRISIL keeps IPCL PCD, NCD programmes ratings AA+.
newsitem.headline: CRISIL keeps IPCL PCD, NCD programmes ratings AA+.

text.p: India's Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) said on Friday it was retaining the 'AA+' rating assigned to the 2.51 billion rupees partly convertible debenture (PCD) programme and 750 million rupees non-convertible debenture (NCD) programme of Indian Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd (IPCL).

The P1+ rating assigned to IPCL's 1,250 million rupees commercial paper programme has also been retained, indicating that the degree of safety regarding timely payment of interest and principal is very strong, CRISIL said.
IPCL is engaged in the manufacture of petrochemicals and polymers such as LDPE, LLDPE, IIDPE, PP, EO/EG, DMT, PVC, PBR, ACN, Acryli fibre.
The company presently has two major integrated petrochemical complexes, one at Vadodara in Gujarat and the second at Nagothane in Maharashtra.

The Vadodara complex uses naphtha as feedstock, which is procured from IOC's refinery situated next to it. The plant at Nagothane is based on natural gas (C2/C3 stream) as feedstock, which is sourced from ONGC's Uran plant.
IPCL is also setting up another integrated petrochemical complex at Dahej, near Bharuch (Gujarat) for manufacture of PVC, EO/EG and HDPE and a jetty for importing essential raw materials.

The complex would use natural gas from the Gandhar gas fields as feedstock. The project which is being implemented in two phases is estimated to cost around 37,000 million. The funding for the above mentioned projects would involve a mix of debt and equity financing and IPCL's leveraging is likely to remain at the existing levels.

The capacity utilisation for the Vadodara and Nagothane complex continue to remain over 90 percent. The business prospects for IPCL are expected to be good in view of the anticipated growth trend for the consumption of polymers and synthetic fibres in India, CRISIL said.
The company also benefits from its wide range of products although, in many products IPCL operates with capacities much lower than the minimum economic size as per international norms.

The company's profit margins are vulnerable to changes in government administered prices of key inputs namely gas and naphtha. IPCL's realisations would also be affected by the reduction in import duty on polymers and various fibre intermediaries despite the marginal cushion resulting on account of depreciation in the value of Indian rupee over the last six months.
IPCL's sales realisations being linked primarily to iInternational prices make it vulnerable to fluctuations in petrochemicals and polymer prices in the global market.

The company has recently raised $175 million through an issue of optionally convertible bonds in the international markets, which would be used to meet the balance fund requirement in completion of the phase II of Gandhar project. IPCL's liquidity position is expected to remain very strong over the next twelve months.
